dedupe_keys.name: mpmas mathematical programming based multi agent system

description: MPMAS is a software package for simulating land-use change in agriculture and forestry, in which each farm household is an agent that decides through whole-farm mathematical programming, coupled with biophysical models of crops, soils and water. It is developed at the University of Hohenheim in Germany. It has been applied in about a dozen countries, including Brazil, Chile, Ethiopia, Germany, Ghana, Thailand, Uganda and Vietnam, for small-scale and large-scale farming systems, usually at the scale of a region or watershed. The site offers a downloads section, but the page read states no licence, version or programming language; the project highlights one-to-one validation of agents and plots against real farms, which suits participatory modelling with farmers. Caveats: models need detailed farm survey data to parameterise every agent, and the optimisation assumption can overstate how rationally farmers react. For simulation it is an agent-based tool for studying how farmers adapt to droughts, water rationing, price shocks or new irrigation infrastructure, and for testing adaptation policies before they are introduced. It is related to the MAGNET record in this catalogue, which models the same pressures at the level of global markets.
